    ```yaml
          over time
      Generator_shut_down_cost:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        description: cost of one stop in this snapshot
      Generator_sign:
        dims: [generator]
        description: the sign output enters its bus's balance with. It is PyPSA's `sign`, `1` unless given,
          `-1` for a unit that draws power. PyPSA refuses one that differs by scenario (`constants.py:46`)
      Generator_stand_by_cost:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        description: cost of one snapshot spent on
      Generator_start_up_cost:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        description: cost of one start in this snapshot
      Generator_status_initial:
        dims: [generator, scenario]
        description: one where the unit was on before the first snapshot, zero where off. It is PyPSA's `up_time_before
          > 0` for a committable unit, and one for a unit that is not, whose ramp rows PyPSA starts from on
          (`constraints.py:323`), data prep. Under a rolling horizon, it is the status the previous window
          solved, a fraction where unit commitment is linearised
      Link_active:
        dims: [link, snapshot]
        dtype: bool
        description: whether a link is active in a snapshot's period. It is PyPSA's `active`, data prep
      Link_active_asset:
        dims: [link]
        dtype: bool
        description: whether a link is one of PyPSA's `active_assets`, by its `active` flag alone, without
          build year and lifetime. A unit that is active in no snapshot of the horizon still counts. PyPSA
          refuses one that differs by scenario (`constants.py:54`)
      Link_committable:
        dims: [link]
        dtype: bool
        description: whether flow is gated by an on/off status decision
      Link_efficiency:
        dims: [link_output, scenario, snapshot]
        description: 'share of the flow that arrives at an output port, PyPSA''s `efficiency`, `efficiency2`,
          … read long: negative where that port consumes rather than delivers. Read at the snapshot the flow
          arrives, so a delayed port delivers at its arrival snapshot''s efficiency (`constraints.py:1575`)'
      Link_marginal_cost:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        description: cost of one unit of flow
      Link_marginal_cost_quadratic:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        description: cost of the square of one unit of flow
      Link_modules_installed:
        dims: [link, scenario]
        description: how many whole modules a committable build has in place, data prep. It is `Link_p_nom
          / Link_p_nom_mod` where a fixed build is modular, and one where it is not. PyPSA refuses a fixed
          modular build whose nominal power is not a whole number of modules
      Link_output_cyclic_delay:
        dims: [link_output]
        dtype: bool
        description: whether a delayed port's flow wraps from the end of its investment period (PyPSA's `cyclic_delay`,
          `cyclic_delay2`, …). Where it does not, the flow still in transit at each period's first snapshots
          is lost. The flag is the same in every scenario, as the delay is
      Link_output_delay:
        dims: [link_output]
        dtype: int
        description: snapshots a port's delivery lags its link's flow (PyPSA's `delay`, `delay2`, … read long).
          In data prep you divide it by the `snapshot_weightings.generators` value and round it up. It is
          zero for a port that delivers at once. A port has the same delay in every scenario, because PyPSA
          refuses a delay that differs by scenario (`constants.py:55`)
      Link_p_init:
        dims: [link, scenario]
        missing: 0.0
        description: the flow a link brought into the horizon, data prep. It is PyPSA's `p_init` where the
          link came in running, and zero where it came in off. Under a rolling horizon, it is the flow the
          previous window solved. No value means it is unknown, and the link then has no ramp row at the first
          snapshot
      Link_p_max_pu:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        description: most flow, per unit of nominal power
      Link_p_min_pu:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        description: 'least flow, per unit of nominal power: negative for a link that carries both ways'
      Link_p_nom:
        dims: [link, scenario]
        description: nominal power
      Link_p_nom_extendable:
        dims: [link]
        dtype: bool
        description: whether the nominal power is a decision
      Link_p_nom_mod:
        dims: [link]
        missing: absent
        description: the module size a build comes in whole numbers of. No value means the build is continuous
      Link_ramp_limit_down:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        missing: absent
        description: most a link may lower its flow between snapshots, per unit of nominal power. No value
          means no limit. The value at the later of the two snapshots applies, so the limit may change over
          time
      Link_ramp_limit_shut_down:
        dims: [link, scenario]
        missing: absent
        description: most flow in the snapshot before a link stops, per unit of nominal power. No value means
          no limit
      Link_ramp_limit_start_up:
        dims: [link, scenario]
        missing: absent
        description: most flow in the snapshot a link starts, per unit of nominal power. No value means no
          limit
      Link_ramp_limit_up:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        missing: absent
        description: most a link may raise its flow between snapshots, per unit of nominal power. No value
          means no limit. The value at the later of the two snapshots applies, so the limit may change over
          time
      Link_shut_down_cost:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        description: cost of one stop in this snapshot
      Link_stand_by_cost:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        description: cost of one snapshot spent on
      Link_start_up_cost:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        description: cost of one start in this snapshot
      Link_status_initial:
        dims: [link, scenario]
        description: one where the link was on before the first snapshot, zero where off. It is PyPSA's `up_time_before
          > 0` for a committable link, and one for a link that is not, whose ramp rows PyPSA starts from on
          (`constraints.py:323`), data prep. Under a rolling horizon, it is the status the previous window
          solved, a fraction where unit commitment is linearised
      Load_active:
        dims: [load]
        dtype: bool
        description: whether a load is active in the network, PyPSA's `active`. A load has no build year and
          no lifetime, so the flag is the same in every snapshot. PyPSA refuses one that differs by scenario
          (`constants.py:54`)
      Load_p_set:
        dims: [load, scenario, snapshot]
        description: demand
      Load_sign:
        dims: [load]
        description: the sign a load's demand enters its bus's balance with. It is PyPSA's `sign`, `-1` unless
          given, `1` for a load that feeds its bus. PyPSA refuses one that differs by scenario (`constants.py:46`)
      Process_active:
        dims: [process, snapshot]
        dtype: bool
        description: whether a process is active in a snapshot's period. It is PyPSA's `active`, data prep
      Process_active_asset:
        dims: [process]
        dtype: bool
        description: whether a process is one of PyPSA's `active_assets`, by its `active` flag alone, without
          build year and lifetime. A unit that is active in no snapshot of the horizon still counts. PyPSA
          refuses one that differs by scenario (`constants.py:54`)
      Process_committable:
        dims: [process]
        dtype: bool
        description: whether internal power is gated by an on/off status decision
      Process_marginal_cost:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        description: cost of one unit of internal power
      Process_marginal_cost_quadratic:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        description: cost of the square of one unit of internal power
      Process_modules_installed:
        dims: [process, scenario]
        description: how many whole modules a committable build has in place, data prep. It is `Process_p_nom
          / Process_p_nom_mod` where a fixed build is modular, and one where it is not. PyPSA refuses a fixed
          modular build whose nominal power is not a whole number of modules
      Process_output_cyclic_delay:
        dims: [process_output]
        dtype: bool
        description: whether a delayed port's transfer wraps from the end of its investment period (PyPSA's
          `cyclic_delay0`, `cyclic_delay1`, …). Where it does not, the energy still in transit at each period's
          first snapshots is lost. The flag is the same in every scenario, as the delay is
      Process_output_delay:
        dims: [process_output]
        dtype: int
        description: snapshots a port's transfer lags its process's internal power (PyPSA's `delay0`, `delay1`,
          … read long). In data prep you divide it by the `snapshot_weightings.generators` value and round
          it up. It is zero for a port that transfers at once. A port has the same delay in every scenario,
          as a link's port has
      Process_p_init:
        dims: [process, scenario]
        missing: 0.0
        description: the internal power a process brought into the horizon, data prep. It is PyPSA's `p_init`
          where the process came in running, and zero where it came in off. Under a rolling horizon, it is
          the internal power the previous window solved. No value means it is unknown, and the process then
          has no ramp row at the first snapshot
      Process_p_max_pu:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        description: most internal power, per unit of nominal power
      Process_p_min_pu:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        description: 'least internal power, per unit of nominal power: negative for a process that runs both
          ways'
      Process_p_nom:
        dims: [process, scenario]
        description: nominal internal power
      Process_p_nom_extendable:
        dims: [process]
        dtype: bool
        description: whether the nominal internal power is a decision
      Process_p_nom_mod:
        dims: [process]
        missing: absent
        description: the module size a build comes in whole numbers of. No value means the build is continuous
      Process_ramp_limit_down:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        missing: absent
        description: most a process may lower its internal power between snapshots, per unit of nominal power.
          No value means no limit. The value at the later of the two snapshots applies, so the limit may change
          over time
      Process_ramp_limit_shut_down:
        dims: [process, scenario]
        missing: absent
        description: most internal power in the snapshot before a process stops, per unit of nominal power.
          No value means no limit
      Process_ramp_limit_start_up:
        dims: [process, scenario]
        missing: absent
        description: most internal power in the snapshot a process starts, per unit of nominal power. No value
          means no limit
      Process_ramp_limit_up:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        missing: absent
        description: most a process may raise its internal power between snapshots, per unit of nominal power.
          No value means no limit. The value at the later of the two snapshots applies, so the limit may change
          over time
      Process_rate:
        dims: [process_output, scenario, snapshot]
        description: the energy a port draws or delivers per unit of internal power (PyPSA's `rate0`, `rate1`,
          … read long). It is negative where the port withdraws and positive where it injects. A link is a
          process whose `bus0` rate is minus one and whose output rates are its efficiencies. The rate at
          the snapshot the transfer arrives applies, so a delayed port transfers at its arrival snapshot's
          rate (`constraints.py:1575`)
      Process_shut_down_cost:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        description: cost of one stop in this snapshot
      Process_stand_by_cost:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        description: cost of one snapshot spent on
      Process_start_up_cost:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        description: cost of one start in this snapshot
      Process_status_initial:
        dims: [process, scenario]
        description: one where the process was on before the first snapshot, zero where off. It is PyPSA's
          `up_time_before > 0` for a committable process, and one for a process that is not, whose ramp rows
          PyPSA starts from on (`constraints.py:323`), data prep. Under a rolling horizon, it is the status
          the previous window solved, a fraction where unit commitment is linearised
      period_weight_objective:
        dims: [period]
        description: PyPSA's `investment_period_weightings.objective` — what a period's cost weighs. PyPSA
          reads it only under `multi_investment_periods`. Otherwise you feed one in data prep, whatever the
          column contains (`optimize.py:231-233`, `:293-297`)
      scenario_weight:
        dims: [scenario]
        description: PyPSA's `scenario_weightings.weight` — the probability of a future
      snapshot_weightings_objective:
        dims: [snapshot]
        description: PyPSA's `snapshot_weightings.objective` — hours a snapshot weighs in the cost
    variables:
      Generator_p:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Generator_active
        description: '`Generator-p` — output of a generator in a snapshot'
      Generator_shut_down:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Generator_committed
        bounds: {lower: 0.0}
        domain: integer
        description: '`Generator-shut_down` — how much of a committable unit turns off this snapshot, capped
          as the status is'
      Generator_start_up:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Generator_committed
        bounds: {lower: 0.0}
        domain: integer
        description: '`Generator-start_up` — how much of a committable unit turns on this snapshot, capped
          as the status is'
      Generator_status:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Generator_committed
        bounds: {lower: 0.0}
        domain: integer
        description: '`Generator-status` — how much of a committable unit is on. It is an integer the rows
          below cap at one, or at the module count where the build is modular'
      Link_p:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Link_active
        description: '`Link-p` — PyPSA''s `p0`, the flow measured at the `Link_bus0` end. A positive value
          withdraws there and injects at every bus the link''s output ports deliver to'
      Link_shut_down:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Link_committed
        bounds: {lower: 0.0}
        domain: integer
        description: '`Link-shut_down` — how much of a committable link turns off this snapshot, capped as
          the status is'
      Link_start_up:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Link_committed
        bounds: {lower: 0.0}
        domain: integer
        description: '`Link-start_up` — how much of a committable link turns on this snapshot, capped as the
          status is'
      Link_status:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Link_committed
        bounds: {lower: 0.0}
        domain: integer
        description: '`Link-status` — how much of a committable link is on. It is an integer the rows below
          cap at one, or at the module count where the build is modular'
      Process_p:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Process_active
        description: '`Process-p` — PyPSA''s internal power `p`. A positive value drives every port at its
          own rate, withdrawing where the rate is negative and injecting where it is positive'
      Process_shut_down:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Process_committed
        bounds: {lower: 0.0}
        domain: integer
        description: '`Process-shut_down` — how much of a committable process turns off this snapshot, capped
          as the status is'
      Process_start_up:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Process_committed
        bounds: {lower: 0.0}
        domain: integer
        description: '`Process-start_up` — how much of a committable process turns on this snapshot, capped
          as the status is'
      Process_status:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Process_committed
        bounds: {lower: 0.0}
        domain: integer
        description: '`Process-status` — how much of a committable process is on. It is an integer the rows
          below cap at one, or at the module count where the build is modular'
      Generator_p_nom_ext:
        dims: [generator]
        where: Generator_p_nom_extendable AND Generator_active_asset
        description: '`Generator-p_nom` — nominal power where it is a decision, for a generator that is active.
          A fixed build is the parameter of the same PyPSA name'
      Link_p_nom_ext:
        dims: [link]
        where: Link_p_nom_extendable AND Link_active_asset
        description: '`Link-p_nom` — nominal power where it is a decision, for a link that is active. A fixed
          build is the parameter of the same PyPSA name'
      Process_p_nom_ext:
        dims: [process]
        where: Process_p_nom_extendable AND Process_active_asset
        description: '`Process-p_nom` — nominal internal power where it is a decision, for a process that
          is active. A fixed build is the parameter of the same PyPSA name'
      Generator_marginal_cost_piecewise:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Generator_marginal_cost_curve AND Generator_active
        description: '`Generator-marginal_cost_piecewise` — the running cost of a generator that pays along
          a curve, held above the curve'
    constraints:
      Bus_nodal_balance:
        dims: [bus, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Bus_attached
        expression: Bus_injection == 0
        description: '`Bus-nodal_balance` — what is generated at a bus meets the load there, less half of
          every incident line''s and transformer''s loss. What is generated includes storage dispatch and
          stores. It is net of what the links take away, plus what arrives over them after losses and any
          delay at every port they deliver to. Each process port draws or delivers at its own rate, and each
          passive branch carries its flow. PyPSA dissipates a branch''s loss half at either end. Each generator,
          storage unit, store and load term enters with its component''s `sign` (`constraints.py:1480-1481`,
          `:1592`), and an inactive load not at all. A bus nothing is attached to has no row. PyPSA refuses
          one that carries load. The file states no assumption for it.'
      Generator_com_p_lower:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Generator_committed AND NOT Generator_p_nom_extendable AND NOT (Generator_p_nom_mod > 0)
        expression: Generator_p >= (Generator_p_min_pu * Generator_p_nom) * Generator_status
        description: '`Generator-com-p-lower` — a committed unit outputs at least its minimum. Off, it outputs
          at least nothing'
      Generator_com_p_upper:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Generator_committed AND NOT Generator_p_nom_extendable AND NOT (Generator_p_nom_mod > 0)
        expression: Generator_p <= (Generator_p_max_pu * Generator_p_nom) * Generator_status
        description: '`Generator-com-p-upper` — a committed unit outputs at most what is available. Off, it
          outputs at most nothing'
      Generator_com_transition_shut_down:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Generator_committed
        expression: Generator_shut_down >= Generator_previous_status - Generator_status
        description: '`Generator-com-transition-shut-down` — turning off is a stop, counted against the state
          the unit carried into the snapshot'
      Generator_com_transition_start_up:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Generator_committed
        expression: Generator_start_up >= Generator_status - Generator_previous_status
        description: '`Generator-com-transition-start-up` — turning on is a start, counted against the state
          the unit carried into the snapshot'
      Generator_fix_p_lower:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        where: not Generator_p_nom_extendable AND not Generator_committable AND Generator_active
        expression: Generator_p >= Generator_p_min_pu * Generator_p_nom
        description: '`Generator-fix-p-lower` — a fixed generator outputs at least its minimum'
      Generator_fix_p_upper:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        where: not Generator_p_nom_extendable AND not Generator_committable AND Generator_active
        expression: Generator_p <= Generator_p_max_pu * Generator_p_nom
        description: '`Generator-fix-p-upper` — a fixed generator outputs at most what is available'
      Generator_p_ramp_limit_down:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        where: (Generator_ramp_limit_down OR Generator_ramp_limit_shut_down) AND NOT (Generator_committable
          AND Generator_p_nom_extendable AND NOT (Generator_p_nom_mod > 0)) AND Generator_ramps_from_previous
          AND Generator_active
        expression: Generator_previous_p - Generator_p <= Generator_ramp_down_allowance
        description: '`Generator-p-ramp_limit_down` — a generator lowers output no faster than its ramp limit
          of the build. A committed one lowers it no further than its shut-down ramp in the snapshot it turns
          off. A unit that came into the horizon running has a row at the first snapshot only where its `p_init`
          gives the output it brought in. No unit has one at the start of a later investment period, nor does
          any unit a big M releases instead'
      Generator_p_ramp_limit_up:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        where: (Generator_ramp_limit_up OR Generator_ramp_limit_start_up) AND NOT (Generator_committable AND
          Generator_p_nom_extendable AND NOT (Generator_p_nom_mod > 0)) AND Generator_ramps_from_previous
          AND Generator_active
        expression: Generator_p - Generator_previous_p <= Generator_ramp_up_allowance
        description: '`Generator-p-ramp_limit_up` — a generator raises output no faster than its ramp limit
          of the build. A committed one raises it no further than its start-up ramp in the snapshot it turns
          on. A unit that came into the horizon running has a row at the first snapshot only where its `p_init`
          gives the output it brought in. No unit has one at the start of a later investment period, nor does
          any unit a big M releases instead'
      Generator_shut_down_p_fixed_upper:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Generator_committed AND NOT (Generator_p_nom_extendable AND Generator_p_nom_mod > 0)
        expression: Generator_shut_down <= Generator_modules_installed
        description: '`Generator-shut_down-p-fixed-upper` — a stop is at most the modules in place, an explicit
          row as PyPSA writes it. The bound is one where the build is not modular, and the fixed build''s
          whole count of modules where it is'
      Generator_start_up_p_fixed_upper:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Generator_committed AND NOT (Generator_p_nom_extendable AND Generator_p_nom_mod > 0)
        expression: Generator_start_up <= Generator_modules_installed
        description: '`Generator-start_up-p-fixed-upper` — a start is at most the modules in place, an explicit
          row as PyPSA writes it. The bound is one where the build is not modular, and the fixed build''s
          whole count of modules where it is'
      Generator_status_p_fixed_upper:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Generator_committed AND NOT (Generator_p_nom_extendable AND Generator_p_nom_mod > 0)
        expression: Generator_status <= Generator_modules_installed
        description: '`Generator-status-p-fixed-upper` — a status is at most the modules in place, an explicit
          row as PyPSA writes it. The bound is one where the build is not modular, and the fixed build''s
          whole count of modules where it is'
      Link_com_p_lower:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Link_committed AND NOT Link_p_nom_extendable AND NOT (Link_p_nom_mod > 0)
        expression: Link_p >= (Link_p_min_pu * Link_p_nom) * Link_status
        description: '`Link-com-p-lower` — a committed link flows at least its minimum. Off, it flows at least
          nothing'
      Link_com_p_upper:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Link_committed AND NOT Link_p_nom_extendable AND NOT (Link_p_nom_mod > 0)
        expression: Link_p <= (Link_p_max_pu * Link_p_nom) * Link_status
        description: '`Link-com-p-upper` — a committed link flows at most what is available. Off, it flows
          at most nothing'
      Link_com_transition_shut_down:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Link_committed
        expression: Link_shut_down >= Link_previous_status - Link_status
        description: '`Link-com-transition-shut-down` — turning off is a stop, counted against the state the
          link carried into the snapshot'
      Link_com_transition_start_up:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Link_committed
        expression: Link_start_up >= Link_status - Link_previous_status
        description: '`Link-com-transition-start-up` — turning on is a start, counted against the state the
          link carried into the snapshot'
      Link_fix_p_lower:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        where: not Link_p_nom_extendable AND not Link_committable AND Link_active
        expression: Link_p >= Link_p_min_pu * Link_p_nom
        description: '`Link-fix-p-lower` — a fixed link carries at least its minimum, negative for the other
          way'
      Link_fix_p_upper:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        where: not Link_p_nom_extendable AND not Link_committable AND Link_active
        expression: Link_p <= Link_p_max_pu * Link_p_nom
        description: '`Link-fix-p-upper` — a fixed link carries at most its nominal power'
      Link_p_ramp_limit_down:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        where: (Link_ramp_limit_down OR Link_ramp_limit_shut_down) AND NOT (Link_committable AND Link_p_nom_extendable
          AND NOT (Link_p_nom_mod > 0)) AND Link_ramps_from_previous AND Link_active
        expression: Link_previous_p - Link_p <= Link_ramp_down_allowance
        description: '`Link-p-ramp_limit_down` — a link lowers flow no faster than its ramp limit of the build.
          A committed one lowers it no further than its shut-down ramp in the snapshot it turns off. A link
          that came into the horizon running has a row at the first snapshot only where its `p_init` gives
          the flow it brought in. No link has one at the start of a later investment period, nor does any
          link a big M releases instead'
      Link_p_ramp_limit_up:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        where: (Link_ramp_limit_up OR Link_ramp_limit_start_up) AND NOT (Link_committable AND Link_p_nom_extendable
          AND NOT (Link_p_nom_mod > 0)) AND Link_ramps_from_previous AND Link_active
        expression: Link_p - Link_previous_p <= Link_ramp_up_allowance
        description: '`Link-p-ramp_limit_up` — a link raises flow no faster than its ramp limit of the build.
          A committed one raises it no further than its start-up ramp in the snapshot it turns on. A link
          that came into the horizon running has a row at the first snapshot only where its `p_init` gives
          the flow it brought in. No link has one at the start of a later investment period, nor does any
          link a big M releases instead'
      Link_shut_down_p_fixed_upper:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Link_committed AND NOT (Link_p_nom_extendable AND Link_p_nom_mod > 0)
        expression: Link_shut_down <= Link_modules_installed
        description: '`Link-shut_down-p-fixed-upper` — a stop is at most the modules in place, an explicit
          row as PyPSA writes it. The bound is one where the build is not modular, and the fixed build''s
          whole count of modules where it is'
      Link_start_up_p_fixed_upper:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Link_committed AND NOT (Link_p_nom_extendable AND Link_p_nom_mod > 0)
        expression: Link_start_up <= Link_modules_installed
        description: '`Link-start_up-p-fixed-upper` — a start is at most the modules in place, an explicit
          row as PyPSA writes it. The bound is one where the build is not modular, and the fixed build''s
          whole count of modules where it is'
      Link_status_p_fixed_upper:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Link_committed AND NOT (Link_p_nom_extendable AND Link_p_nom_mod > 0)
        expression: Link_status <= Link_modules_installed
        description: '`Link-status-p-fixed-upper` — a status is at most the modules in place, an explicit
          row as PyPSA writes it. The bound is one where the build is not modular, and the fixed build''s
          whole count of modules where it is'
      Process_com_p_lower:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Process_committed AND NOT Process_p_nom_extendable AND NOT (Process_p_nom_mod > 0)
        expression: Process_p >= (Process_p_min_pu * Process_p_nom) * Process_status
        description: '`Process-com-p-lower` — a committed process runs at least its minimum. Off, it runs
          at least nothing'
      Process_com_p_upper:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Process_committed AND NOT Process_p_nom_extendable AND NOT (Process_p_nom_mod > 0)
        expression: Process_p <= (Process_p_max_pu * Process_p_nom) * Process_status
        description: '`Process-com-p-upper` — a committed process runs at most what is available. Off, it
          runs at most nothing'
      Process_com_transition_shut_down:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Process_committed
        expression: Process_shut_down >= Process_previous_status - Process_status
        description: '`Process-com-transition-shut-down` — turning off is a stop, counted against the state
          the process carried into the snapshot'
      Process_com_transition_start_up:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Process_committed
        expression: Process_start_up >= Process_status - Process_previous_status
        description: '`Process-com-transition-start-up` — turning on is a start, counted against the state
          the process carried into the snapshot'
      Process_p_ramp_limit_down:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        where: (Process_ramp_limit_down OR Process_ramp_limit_shut_down) AND NOT (Process_committable AND
          Process_p_nom_extendable AND NOT (Process_p_nom_mod > 0)) AND Process_ramps_from_previous AND Process_active
        expression: Process_previous_p - Process_p <= Process_ramp_down_allowance
        description: '`Process-p-ramp_limit_down` — a process lowers internal power no faster than its ramp
          limit of the build. A committed one lowers it no further than its shut-down ramp in the snapshot
          it turns off. A process that came into the horizon running has a row at the first snapshot only
          where `p_init` gives the internal power it brought in. No process has one at the start of a later
          investment period, nor does any process a big M releases instead'
      Process_p_ramp_limit_up:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        where: (Process_ramp_limit_up OR Process_ramp_limit_start_up) AND NOT (Process_committable AND Process_p_nom_extendable
          AND NOT (Process_p_nom_mod > 0)) AND Process_ramps_from_previous AND Process_active
        expression: Process_p - Process_previous_p <= Process_ramp_up_allowance
        description: '`Process-p-ramp_limit_up` — a process raises internal power no faster than its ramp
          limit of the build. A committed one raises it no further than its start-up ramp in the snapshot
          it turns on. A process that came into the horizon running has a row at the first snapshot only where
          `p_init` gives the internal power it brought in. No process has one at the start of a later investment
          period, nor does any process a big M releases instead'
      Process_shut_down_p_fixed_upper:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Process_committed AND NOT (Process_p_nom_extendable AND Process_p_nom_mod > 0)
        expression: Process_shut_down <= Process_modules_installed
        description: '`Process-shut_down-p-fixed-upper` — a stop is at most the modules in place, an explicit
          row as PyPSA writes it. The bound is one where the build is not modular, and the fixed build''s
          whole count of modules where it is'
      Process_start_up_p_fixed_upper:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Process_committed AND NOT (Process_p_nom_extendable AND Process_p_nom_mod > 0)
        expression: Process_start_up <= Process_modules_installed
        description: '`Process-start_up-p-fixed-upper` — a start is at most the modules in place, an explicit
          row as PyPSA writes it. The bound is one where the build is not modular, and the fixed build''s
          whole count of modules where it is'
      Process_status_p_fixed_upper:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        where: Process_committed AND NOT (Process_p_nom_extendable AND Process_p_nom_mod > 0)
        expression: Process_status <= Process_modules_installed
        description: '`Process-status-p-fixed-upper` — a status is at most the modules in place, an explicit
          row as PyPSA writes it. The bound is one where the build is not modular, and the fixed build''s
          whole count of modules where it is'
    expressions:
      Bus_injection:
        dims: [bus, scenario, snapshot]
        expression: ((Generator_injection + Link_injection) + Load_injection) + Process_injection
        description: what every component puts into a bus, less what it takes out of it. PyPSA writes each
          term into the balance, and a load on its right-hand side
      Generator_commitment_opex: {expression: 'sum(sum(((Generator_status * Generator_stand_by_cost) * snapshot_weightings_objective)
          * at(period_weight_objective, by=snapshot_period[period]), over=generator), over=snapshot) + sum(sum((Generator_start_up
          * Generator_start_up_cost) * at(period_weight_objective, by=snapshot_period[period]), over=generator),
          over=snapshot) + sum(sum((Generator_shut_down * Generator_shut_down_cost) * at(period_weight_objective,
          by=snapshot_period[period]), over=generator), over=snapshot)'}
      Generator_injection: {expression: 'sum(Generator_sign * Generator_p, over=generator, by=Generator_bus[bus])'}
      Generator_opex: {expression: 'sum(sum((Generator_running_cost * snapshot_weightings_objective) * at(period_weight_objective,
          by=snapshot_period[period]), over=generator), over=snapshot) + sum(sum((((Generator_p * Generator_p)
          * Generator_marginal_cost_quadratic) * snapshot_weightings_objective) * at(period_weight_objective,
          by=snapshot_period[period]), over=generator), over=snapshot)'}
      Generator_p_carried_over:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        description: the output a generator carries over into a snapshot. At the first, it is the `p_init`
          it brought in, which is zero where it came in off. After that, it is the previous snapshot's
        cases:
          opening: {when: position(snapshot) == 0, expression: Generator_p_init}
        otherwise: shift(Generator_p, along=snapshot, offset=1)
      Generator_p_nom_committed:
        dims: [generator, scenario]
        description: 'the build a committed unit''s ramp rows are taken against: one module where the build
          is modular, since its status counts modules, and the given build otherwise (`constraints.py:1131-1134`)'
        cases:
          modular_build: {when: Generator_p_nom_mod > 0, expression: Generator_p_nom_mod}
        otherwise: Generator_p_nom
      Generator_p_nom_effective:
        dims: [generator, scenario]
        description: 'the build a generator''s limits are taken against: the chosen one where it is extendable,
          the given one otherwise'
        cases:
          extendable: {when: Generator_p_nom_extendable, expression: Generator_p_nom_ext}
        otherwise: Generator_p_nom
      Generator_previous_p:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        description: 'the output a generator carries into a snapshot. It is nothing at the first snapshot
          it is active in past the first of the horizon: PyPSA fills an output it did not build with zero
          (`constraints.py:716`). It is the output carried over otherwise'
        cases:
          opening_late: {when: 'position(snapshot) > 0 AND NOT shift(Generator_active, along=snapshot, offset=1)',
            expression: '0'}
        otherwise: Generator_p_carried_over
      Generator_previous_status:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        description: the commitment state a generator carries into a snapshot. It is off at the first snapshot
          it is active in past the first of the horizon. PyPSA reads a status it did not build as off there
          (`constraints.py:391`). It is the state carried over otherwise
        cases:
          opening_late: {when: 'position(snapshot) > 0 AND NOT shift(Generator_active, along=snapshot, offset=1)',
            expression: '0'}
        otherwise: Generator_status_carried_over
      Generator_ramp_down_allowance:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        description: how far a generator may lower output between two snapshots. It is its ramp limit of the
          build while it stays on, plus its shut-down ramp in the snapshot it turns off
        cases:
          committed: {when: Generator_committable, expression: Generator_ramp_down_rate * Generator_p_nom_committed
              * Generator_status + Generator_shut_down_rate * Generator_p_nom_committed * (Generator_ramp_previous_status
              - Generator_status)}
        otherwise: Generator_ramp_down_rate * Generator_p_nom_effective
      Generator_ramp_down_rate:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        description: the ramp limit in a unit's down row, PyPSA's `ramp_limit_down`. It is the full build
          where PyPSA has none, since a shut-down ramp alone builds the row
        cases:
          given: {when: Generator_ramp_limit_down, expression: Generator_ramp_limit_down}
        otherwise: '1'
      Generator_ramp_previous_status:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        description: the status a committed unit's ramp rows carry into a snapshot. At the first snapshot,
          a fixed modular unit that came in running has every module on, since the state it brought in is
          on or off (`constraints.py:1152-1157`). The transition and down-time rows count it as one module
          (PyPSA/PyPSA#2114). It is the state carried in otherwise
        cases:
          opening_modules: {when: position(snapshot) == 0 AND NOT Generator_p_nom_extendable AND Generator_p_nom_mod
              > 0, expression: Generator_status_initial * Generator_modules_installed}
        otherwise: Generator_previous_status
      Generator_ramp_up_allowance:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        description: how far a generator may raise output between two snapshots. It is its ramp limit of the
          build while it stays on, plus its start-up ramp in the snapshot it turns on
        cases:
          committed: {when: Generator_committable, expression: Generator_ramp_up_rate * Generator_p_nom_committed
              * Generator_ramp_previous_status + Generator_start_up_rate * Generator_p_nom_committed * (Generator_status
              - Generator_ramp_previous_status)}
        otherwise: Generator_ramp_up_rate * Generator_p_nom_effective
      Generator_ramp_up_rate:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        description: the ramp limit in a unit's up row, PyPSA's `ramp_limit_up`. It is the full build where
          PyPSA has none, since a start-up ramp alone builds the row
        cases:
          given: {when: Generator_ramp_limit_up, expression: Generator_ramp_limit_up}
        otherwise: '1'
      Generator_running_cost:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        description: 'what a generator''s output costs in a snapshot: the value read off its piecewise curve
          where it has one, and its linear `marginal_cost` otherwise. A curve replaces the linear cost, as
          PyPSA drops the unit from that term (`optimize.py:333-348`)'
        cases:
          curve: {when: Generator_marginal_cost_curve, expression: Generator_marginal_cost_piecewise}
        otherwise: Generator_p * Generator_marginal_cost
      Generator_shut_down_rate:
        dims: [generator, scenario]
        description: the shut-down ramp in a unit's down row (PyPSA's `ramp_limit_shut_down`), or the full
          build where it has none
        cases:
          given: {when: Generator_ramp_limit_shut_down, expression: Generator_ramp_limit_shut_down}
        otherwise: '1'
      Generator_start_up_rate:
        dims: [generator, scenario]
        description: the start-up ramp in a unit's up row (PyPSA's `ramp_limit_start_up`), or the full build
          where it has none
        cases:
          given: {when: Generator_ramp_limit_start_up, expression: Generator_ramp_limit_start_up}
        otherwise: '1'
      Generator_status_carried_over:
        dims: [generator, scenario, snapshot]
        description: 'the state a generator carries over into a snapshot: the state it brought into the horizon
          at the first, the previous snapshot''s after that'
        cases:
          opening: {when: position(snapshot) == 0, expression: Generator_status_initial}
        otherwise: shift(Generator_status, along=snapshot, offset=1)
      Link_commitment_opex: {expression: 'sum(sum(((Link_status * Link_stand_by_cost) * snapshot_weightings_objective)
          * at(period_weight_objective, by=snapshot_period[period]), over=link), over=snapshot) + sum(sum((Link_start_up
          * Link_start_up_cost) * at(period_weight_objective, by=snapshot_period[period]), over=link), over=snapshot)
          + sum(sum((Link_shut_down * Link_shut_down_cost) * at(period_weight_objective, by=snapshot_period[period]),
          over=link), over=snapshot)'}
      Link_injection: {expression: '-sum(Link_p, over=link, by=Link_bus0[bus]) + sum(Link_output_arrival,
          over=link_output, by=Link_output_bus[bus])'}
      Link_opex: {expression: 'sum(sum(((Link_p * Link_marginal_cost) * snapshot_weightings_objective) * at(period_weight_objective,
          by=snapshot_period[period]), over=link), over=snapshot) + sum(sum((((Link_p * Link_p) * Link_marginal_cost_quadratic)
          * snapshot_weightings_objective) * at(period_weight_objective, by=snapshot_period[period]), over=link),
          over=snapshot)'}
      Link_output_arrival:
        dims: [link_output, scenario, snapshot]
        description: what a link delivers to an output port at a snapshot. It is its flow delayed by the port's
          `delay` within its investment period. It is multiplied by the port's efficiency at the snapshot
          the flow arrives. Where the port is `cyclic_delay`, the delayed flow wraps from the period's end.
          Where it is not, the flow still in transit at the period's first snapshots is lost. A port that
          does not delay (`delay` zero) delivers its flow unshifted, cyclic or not
        cases:
          wrapping: {when: Link_output_cyclic_delay, expression: 'shift(at(Link_p, by=Link_output_link[link]),
              along=snapshot, offset=Link_output_delay, edge=''wrap'', within=snapshot_period[period]) * Link_efficiency'}
        otherwise: shift(at(Link_p, by=Link_output_link[link]), along=snapshot, offset=Link_output_delay,
          edge=0, within=snapshot_period[period]) * Link_efficiency
      Link_p_carried_over:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        description: the output a link carries over into a snapshot. At the first, it is the `p_init` it brought
          in, which is zero where it came in off. After that, it is the previous snapshot's
        cases:
          opening: {when: position(snapshot) == 0, expression: Link_p_init}
        otherwise: shift(Link_p, along=snapshot, offset=1)
      Link_p_nom_committed:
        dims: [link, scenario]
        description: 'the build a committed link''s ramp rows are taken against: one module where the build
          is modular, since its status counts modules, and the given build otherwise (`constraints.py:1131-1134`)'
        cases:
          modular_build: {when: Link_p_nom_mod > 0, expression: Link_p_nom_mod}
        otherwise: Link_p_nom
      Link_p_nom_effective:
        dims: [link, scenario]
        description: 'the build a link''s limits are taken against: the chosen one where it is extendable,
          the given one otherwise'
        cases:
          extendable: {when: Link_p_nom_extendable, expression: Link_p_nom_ext}
        otherwise: Link_p_nom
      Link_previous_p:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        description: 'the output a link carries into a snapshot. It is nothing at the first snapshot it is
          active in past the first of the horizon: PyPSA fills an output it did not build with zero (`constraints.py:716`).
          It is the output carried over otherwise'
        cases:
          opening_late: {when: 'position(snapshot) > 0 AND NOT shift(Link_active, along=snapshot, offset=1)',
            expression: '0'}
        otherwise: Link_p_carried_over
      Link_previous_status:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        description: the commitment state a link carries into a snapshot. It is off at the first snapshot
          it is active in past the first of the horizon. PyPSA reads a status it did not build as off there
          (`constraints.py:391`). It is the state carried over otherwise
        cases:
          opening_late: {when: 'position(snapshot) > 0 AND NOT shift(Link_active, along=snapshot, offset=1)',
            expression: '0'}
        otherwise: Link_status_carried_over
      Link_ramp_down_allowance:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        description: how far a link may lower flow between two snapshots. It is its ramp limit of the build
          while it stays on, plus its shut-down ramp in the snapshot it turns off
        cases:
          committed: {when: Link_committable, expression: Link_ramp_down_rate * Link_p_nom_committed * Link_status
              + Link_shut_down_rate * Link_p_nom_committed * (Link_ramp_previous_status - Link_status)}
        otherwise: Link_ramp_down_rate * Link_p_nom_effective
      Link_ramp_down_rate:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        description: the ramp limit in a link's down row, PyPSA's `ramp_limit_down`. It is the full build
          where PyPSA has none, since a shut-down ramp alone builds the row
        cases:
          given: {when: Link_ramp_limit_down, expression: Link_ramp_limit_down}
        otherwise: '1'
      Link_ramp_previous_status:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        description: the status a committed link's ramp rows carry into a snapshot. At the first snapshot,
          a fixed modular link that came in running has every module on, since the state it brought in is
          on or off (`constraints.py:1152-1157`). The transition and down-time rows count it as one module
          (PyPSA/PyPSA#2114). It is the state carried in otherwise
        cases:
          opening_modules: {when: position(snapshot) == 0 AND NOT Link_p_nom_extendable AND Link_p_nom_mod
              > 0, expression: Link_status_initial * Link_modules_installed}
        otherwise: Link_previous_status
      Link_ramp_up_allowance:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        description: how far a link may raise flow between two snapshots. It is its ramp limit of the build
          while it stays on, plus its start-up ramp in the snapshot it turns on
        cases:
          committed: {when: Link_committable, expression: Link_ramp_up_rate * Link_p_nom_committed * Link_ramp_previous_status
              + Link_start_up_rate * Link_p_nom_committed * (Link_status - Link_ramp_previous_status)}
        otherwise: Link_ramp_up_rate * Link_p_nom_effective
      Link_ramp_up_rate:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        description: the ramp limit in a link's up row, PyPSA's `ramp_limit_up`. It is the full build where
          PyPSA has none, since a start-up ramp alone builds the row
        cases:
          given: {when: Link_ramp_limit_up, expression: Link_ramp_limit_up}
        otherwise: '1'
      Link_shut_down_rate:
        dims: [link, scenario]
        description: the shut-down ramp in a link's down row (PyPSA's `ramp_limit_shut_down`), or the full
          build where it has none
        cases:
          given: {when: Link_ramp_limit_shut_down, expression: Link_ramp_limit_shut_down}
        otherwise: '1'
      Link_start_up_rate:
        dims: [link, scenario]
        description: the start-up ramp in a link's up row (PyPSA's `ramp_limit_start_up`), or the full build
          where it has none
        cases:
          given: {when: Link_ramp_limit_start_up, expression: Link_ramp_limit_start_up}
        otherwise: '1'
      Link_status_carried_over:
        dims: [link, scenario, snapshot]
        description: 'the state a link carries over into a snapshot: the state it brought into the horizon
          at the first, the previous snapshot''s after that'
        cases:
          opening: {when: position(snapshot) == 0, expression: Link_status_initial}
        otherwise: shift(Link_status, along=snapshot, offset=1)
      Load_demand:
        dims: [load, scenario, snapshot]
        description: what a load draws from its bus's balance. It is its demand times its sign where it is
          active, and nothing where it is not. PyPSA drops an inactive load from the balance (`constraints.py:1591-1592`)
        cases:
          active: {when: Load_active, expression: Load_sign * Load_p_set}
        otherwise: '0'
      Load_injection: {expression: 'sum(Load_demand, over=load, by=Load_bus[bus])'}
      Process_commitment_opex: {expression: 'sum(sum(((Process_status * Process_stand_by_cost) * snapshot_weightings_objective)
          * at(period_weight_objective, by=snapshot_period[period]), over=process), over=snapshot) + sum(sum((Process_start_up
          * Process_start_up_cost) * at(period_weight_objective, by=snapshot_period[period]), over=process),
          over=snapshot) + sum(sum((Process_shut_down * Process_shut_down_cost) * at(period_weight_objective,
          by=snapshot_period[period]), over=process), over=snapshot)'}
      Process_injection: {expression: 'sum(Process_output_arrival, over=process_output, by=Process_output_bus[bus])'}
      Process_opex: {expression: 'sum(sum(((Process_p * Process_marginal_cost) * snapshot_weightings_objective)
          * at(period_weight_objective, by=snapshot_period[period]), over=process), over=snapshot) + sum(sum((((Process_p
          * Process_p) * Process_marginal_cost_quadratic) * snapshot_weightings_objective) * at(period_weight_objective,
          by=snapshot_period[period]), over=process), over=snapshot)'}
      Process_output_arrival:
        dims: [process_output, scenario, snapshot]
        description: what a process transfers at a port at a snapshot. It is its internal power delayed by
          the port's `delay` within its investment period. It is multiplied by the port's rate at the snapshot
          the transfer arrives. Where the port is `cyclic_delay`, the delayed transfer wraps from the period's
          end. Where it is not, the energy still in transit at the period's first snapshots is lost. A port
          that does not delay (`delay` zero) transfers at once, cyclic or not
        cases:
          wrapping: {when: Process_output_cyclic_delay, expression: 'shift(at(Process_p, by=Process_output_process[process]),
              along=snapshot, offset=Process_output_delay, edge=''wrap'', within=snapshot_period[period])
              * Process_rate'}
        otherwise: shift(at(Process_p, by=Process_output_process[process]), along=snapshot, offset=Process_output_delay,
          edge=0, within=snapshot_period[period]) * Process_rate
      Process_p_carried_over:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        description: the output a process carries over into a snapshot. At the first, it is the `p_init` it
          brought in, which is zero where it came in off. After that, it is the previous snapshot's
        cases:
          opening: {when: position(snapshot) == 0, expression: Process_p_init}
        otherwise: shift(Process_p, along=snapshot, offset=1)
      Process_p_nom_committed:
        dims: [process, scenario]
        description: 'the build a committed process''s ramp rows are taken against: one module where the build
          is modular, since its status counts modules, and the given build otherwise (`constraints.py:1131-1134`)'
        cases:
          modular_build: {when: Process_p_nom_mod > 0, expression: Process_p_nom_mod}
        otherwise: Process_p_nom
      Process_p_nom_effective:
        dims: [process, scenario]
        description: 'the build a process''s limits are taken against: the chosen one where it is extendable,
          the given one otherwise'
        cases:
          extendable: {when: Process_p_nom_extendable, expression: Process_p_nom_ext}
        otherwise: Process_p_nom
      Process_previous_p:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        description: 'the output a process carries into a snapshot. It is nothing at the first snapshot it
          is active in past the first of the horizon: PyPSA fills an output it did not build with zero (`constraints.py:716`).
          It is the output carried over otherwise'
        cases:
          opening_late: {when: 'position(snapshot) > 0 AND NOT shift(Process_active, along=snapshot, offset=1)',
            expression: '0'}
        otherwise: Process_p_carried_over
      Process_previous_status:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        description: the commitment state a process carries into a snapshot. It is off at the first snapshot
          it is active in past the first of the horizon. PyPSA reads a status it did not build as off there
          (`constraints.py:391`). It is the state carried over otherwise
        cases:
          opening_late: {when: 'position(snapshot) > 0 AND NOT shift(Process_active, along=snapshot, offset=1)',
            expression: '0'}
        otherwise: Process_status_carried_over
      Process_ramp_down_allowance:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        description: how far a process may lower internal power between two snapshots. It is its ramp limit
          of the build while it stays on, plus its shut-down ramp in the snapshot it turns off
        cases:
          committed: {when: Process_committable, expression: Process_ramp_down_rate * Process_p_nom_committed
              * Process_status + Process_shut_down_rate * Process_p_nom_committed * (Process_ramp_previous_status
              - Process_status)}
        otherwise: Process_ramp_down_rate * Process_p_nom_effective
      Process_ramp_down_rate:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        description: the ramp limit in a process's down row, PyPSA's `ramp_limit_down`. It is the full build
          where PyPSA has none, since a shut-down ramp alone builds the row
        cases:
          given: {when: Process_ramp_limit_down, expression: Process_ramp_limit_down}
        otherwise: '1'
      Process_ramp_previous_status:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        description: the status a committed process's ramp rows carry into a snapshot. At the first snapshot,
          a fixed modular process that came in running has every module on, since the state it brought in
          is on or off (`constraints.py:1152-1157`). The transition and down-time rows count it as one module
          (PyPSA/PyPSA#2114). It is the state carried in otherwise
        cases:
          opening_modules: {when: position(snapshot) == 0 AND NOT Process_p_nom_extendable AND Process_p_nom_mod
              > 0, expression: Process_status_initial * Process_modules_installed}
        otherwise: Process_previous_status
      Process_ramp_up_allowance:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        description: how far a process may raise internal power between two snapshots. It is its ramp limit
          of the build while it stays on, plus its start-up ramp in the snapshot it turns on
        cases:
          committed: {when: Process_committable, expression: Process_ramp_up_rate * Process_p_nom_committed
              * Process_ramp_previous_status + Process_start_up_rate * Process_p_nom_committed * (Process_status
              - Process_ramp_previous_status)}
        otherwise: Process_ramp_up_rate * Process_p_nom_effective
      Process_ramp_up_rate:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        description: the ramp limit in a process's up row, PyPSA's `ramp_limit_up`. It is the full build where
          PyPSA has none, since a start-up ramp alone builds the row
        cases:
          given: {when: Process_ramp_limit_up, expression: Process_ramp_limit_up}
        otherwise: '1'
      Process_shut_down_rate:
        dims: [process, scenario]
        description: the shut-down ramp in a process's down row (PyPSA's `ramp_limit_shut_down`), or the full
          build where it has none
        cases:
          given: {when: Process_ramp_limit_shut_down, expression: Process_ramp_limit_shut_down}
        otherwise: '1'
      Process_start_up_rate:
        dims: [process, scenario]
        description: the start-up ramp in a process's up row (PyPSA's `ramp_limit_start_up`), or the full
          build where it has none
        cases:
          given: {when: Process_ramp_limit_start_up, expression: Process_ramp_limit_start_up}
        otherwise: '1'
      Process_status_carried_over:
        dims: [process, scenario, snapshot]
        description: 'the state a process carries over into a snapshot: the state it brought into the horizon
          at the first, the previous snapshot''s after that'
        cases:
          opening: {when: position(snapshot) == 0, expression: Process_status_initial}
        otherwise: shift(Process_status, along=snapshot, offset=1)
      risk_weighted_opex: {expression: 'sum(scenario_weight * scenario_opex, over=scenario)'}
      scenario_opex:
        dims: [scenario]
        expression: ((((Generator_opex + Generator_commitment_opex) + Link_opex) + Link_commitment_opex) +
          Process_opex) + Process_commitment_opex
        description: 'what a future costs to run: every operating term, weighted by the snapshot''s hours
          and its period, before the scenario''s own weight. A start and a stop cost what they cost, unweighted,
          as PyPSA adds them (`optimize.py:448-468`)'
      total_cost:
        dims: []
        expression: risk_weighted_opex
        description: what the system costs. Capacity counts once per active period at its expected cost over
          the scenarios. Operation counts in expectation over the scenarios, and a share of it at the tail
    conditions:
      Generator_committed: {condition: Generator_committable AND Generator_active, description: 'a committable
          generator that is active in the snapshot''s period: every unit-commitment row''s set'}
      Generator_marginal_cost_curve: {condition: 'count(Generator_marginal_cost_curve_p, over=breakpoint)
          > 0 AND Generator_active_asset', description: 'a generator that pays along a piecewise `marginal_cost`
          curve: one of PyPSA''s `active_assets` with curve data (`optimize.py:307`, `piecewise.py:230-257`)'}
      Generator_ramps_from_previous: {condition: 'position(snapshot, within=snapshot_period[period]) > 0 OR
          (position(snapshot) == 0 AND (Generator_status_initial == 0 OR Generator_p_init))', description: 'a
          snapshot whose ramp uses a previous output. It is any snapshot but its period''s first, and the
          horizon''s first where the generator comes in off or carries an initial output'}
      Link_committed: {condition: Link_committable AND Link_active, description: 'a committable link that
          is active in the snapshot''s period: every unit-commitment row''s set'}
      Link_ramps_from_previous: {condition: 'position(snapshot, within=snapshot_period[period]) > 0 OR (position(snapshot)
          == 0 AND (Link_status_initial == 0 OR Link_p_init))', description: 'a snapshot whose ramp uses a
          previous output. It is any snapshot but its period''s first, and the horizon''s first where the
          link comes in off or carries an initial output'}
      Process_committed: {condition: Process_committable AND Process_active, description: 'a committable process
          that is active in the snapshot''s period: every unit-commitment row''s set'}
      Process_ramps_from_previous: {condition: 'position(snapshot, within=snapshot_period[period]) > 0 OR
          (position(snapshot) == 0 AND (Process_status_initial == 0 OR Process_p_init))', description: 'a
          snapshot whose ramp uses a previous output. It is any snapshot but its period''s first, and the
          horizon''s first where the process comes in off or carries an initial output'}
    objective: {sense: minimize, expression: total_cost}
    ```

    ```python
    from differential.pypsa.prep import relation, static, varying, weighting


    n = build()  # the network from the PyPSA tab

    sources = {
        'bus': pl.Series('bus', list(names(n.buses.index).astype(str)), dtype=pl.String),
            **{
                dim: pl.Series(dim, list(names(n.static(component).index).astype(str)), dtype=pl.String)
                for component, dim in DIM.items()
            },
            **scenarios(n),
            **periods(n, multi),
            **carriers(n, multi),
        'snapshot': pl.Series('snapshot', list(timesteps(n)), dtype=pl.Datetime('us')),
        'Generator_bus': relation(n, 'Generator', 'bus'),
        'Link_bus0': relation(n, 'Link', 'bus0'),
        'Load_bus': relation(n, 'Load', 'bus'),
        'Bus_attached': attached(n),
        'Generator_sign': per_component('Generator', first_scenario(n.generators['sign'])),
        'Load_active': per_component('Load', first_scenario(loads['active']), bool),
        'Load_p_set': varying(n, 'Load', 'p_set'),
        'Load_sign': per_component('Load', first_scenario(loads['sign'])),
        'snapshot_weightings_objective': weighting(n, 'objective'),
    }

    with sps.solve('differential/pypsa/rungs/rung_28_start_up_ramp.yaml', sources) as result:
        result.objective  # 83283.0
    ```

=== "PyPSA"

    The network, `rung_28_start_up_ramp.py` in the corpus — the spine plus what this rung adds:

    ```python
    # SPDX-FileCopyrightText: mathspec Contributors
    #
    # SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

    """Rung 28: a start-up ramp alone — a committable unit with only a start-up and a shut-down ramp still gets ramp rows, at the full build between them."""

    from __future__ import annotations

    import spine


    def build():
        """The spine plus a pulse bus served by committable generator, link and process that carry only start-up and shut-down ramps, with a dear backup."""
        n = spine.build()
        n.add('Bus', 'pulse')
        common = {
            'committable': True,
            'p_nom': 40,
            'p_min_pu': 0.1,
            'up_time_before': 0,
            'ramp_limit_start_up': 0.4,
            'ramp_limit_shut_down': 0.5,
        }
        n.add('Generator', 'pulse_gen', bus='pulse', marginal_cost=3, **common)
        n.add('Link', 'pulse_link', bus0='north', bus1='pulse', marginal_cost=4, **common)
        n.add('Process', 'pulse_proc', bus0='south', bus1='pulse', rate0=-1.25, marginal_cost=5, **common)
        n.add('Generator', 'pulse_backup', bus='pulse', p_nom=200, marginal_cost=500)
        n.add('Load', 'pulse_load', bus='pulse', p_set=[0, 60, 110, 0])
        return n
    ```

    ```python
    n = build()
    n.optimize(solver_name='highs')
    n.objective  # 83283.0
    ```
